pp:ce:2011:q1.title: GATE CE 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 1
pp:ce:2011:q1.question: [A] is a square matrix which is neither symmetric nor skew-symmetric and $[A]^{T}$ is its transpose. The sum and difference of these matrices are defined as $[S] = [A]+[A]^{T}$ and $[D] = [A]-[A]^{T}$, respectively. Which of the following statements is TRUE?

detailed_solution.markdown:
Since

$$\begin{aligned} \left ( A+{A}' \right )&=A^{t}+\left ( A^{t} \right )^{t} \\      &=A^{t}+A\\ \text{i.e. }     S^{t}&=S \\ \therefore\;\; & \text{ S is symmetric}\\ \text{Since }\left ( A-A^{t} \right )^{t}&=A^{t}-\left ( A^{t} \right )^{t} \\      &=A^{t}-A \\ &=-\left ( A-A^{t} \right ) \\ \text{i.e. }     D^{t}&=-D \end{aligned}$$

So D is Skew-Symmetric.

pp:ce:2011:q2.title: GATE CE 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 2
pp:ce:2011:q2.question:
The square root of a number N is to be obtained by applying the Newton
Raphson iterations to the equation $x^2-N=0$. If i denotes the iteration index,
the correct iterative scheme will be

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned}   x_{i+1}&=x_{i}-\frac{f\left ( x_{i} \right )}{{f}'\left ( x_{i} \right )} \\      &=x_{i}-\left ( \frac{x_{i}^{2}-N}{2x_{i}} \right ) \\      &=\frac{x_{i}^{2}+N}{2x_{i}} \\ &=\frac{1}{2}\left [ x_{i}+\frac{N}{x_{i}} \right ] \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2011:q26.title: GATE CE 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 26
pp:ce:2011:q26.question: For an analytic function, $f(x + iy) = u(x,y)+ iv(x,y), \; u$ is given by $u = 3x^{2}-3y^{2}$. The expression for $v$, considering $K$ to be a constant is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$f=u+iv \text{ and }   u=3x^{2}-3y^{2}$

For $f$ to be analysis, we have Cauchy-Riemann conditions,

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}&=\frac{\partial V}{\partial y}  \;\;\;...(i) \\   \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}&=-\frac{\partial v}{\partial x} \;\;\;...(ii)\\ \text{From } & \text{ (i) we have,}\\   6x&=\frac{\partial v}{\partial y} \\ \Rightarrow \;  \int \partial v&=\int 6x\partial y \\   v&=6\frac{x^{2}}{2}+f\left ( x \right )\\ \text{i.e., } v&=3x^{2}+f\left ( x \right )\;\;...(iii)\\ \text{Now applying }&\text{equation (ii) we get,}\\  \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}&=-\frac{\partial v}{\partial x} \\ \Rightarrow  \; \; -6y&=-\left [ 6x+\frac{df}{dx} \right ]\\ \Rightarrow \;\; 6x+\frac{df}{dx}&=6y \\   \frac{df}{dx}&=6y-6x \\ &\text{By integrating,}\\ f\left ( x \right )&=6yx-3x^{2}+K\\ \text{Substitute }& \text{in equation (iii),}\\  v&=3x^{2}+6yx-3x^{2}+K \\ \Rightarrow  \;\; v&=6yx+K \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2011:q27.title: GATE CE 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 27
pp:ce:2011:q27.question:
What should be the value of $\lambda$ such that the function defined below is continuous at $x = \pi /2$?
$$f(x)=\left\{\begin{matrix} \frac{\lambda \cos x}{\frac{\pi }{2}-x} &if x \neq \frac{\pi }{2} \\ 1& if x= \frac{\pi }{2} \end{matrix}\right.$$

detailed_solution.markdown:
if f(x) is continuous at $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$

$\lim_{x\rightarrow \frac{\pi }{2}}\frac{\lambda \cos x}{\frac{\pi }{2}-x}=f\left ( \frac{\pi }{2} \right )=1$

Since the limit is in form of $\frac{0}{0}$, we can use L'Hospitals rule on LHS of equation (i) and get

$$\begin{aligned} \lim_{x\rightarrow \frac{\pi }{2}}\frac{-\lambda \sin x}{-1}&=1 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; \lambda \sin \frac{\pi }{2}&=1 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; \lambda &=1\end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2011:q28.title: GATE CE 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 28
pp:ce:2011:q28.question: What is the value of the definite integral, $\int_{0}^{a}\frac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{a-x}}dx$ ?

detailed_solution.markdown:
Let

$$\begin{aligned}  I&=\int_{0}^{a}\frac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{a-x}} dx \;\;  ...(i) \\ \text{Since } \int_{0}^{a}f\left ( x \right )dx&=\int_{0}^{a}f\left ( a-x \right )dx \\    I&=\int_{0}^{a}\frac{\sqrt{a-x}}{\sqrt{a-x}+\sqrt{x}}dx \;\; ...(ii)\\ (i)+(ii) \; \Rightarrow \; 2I&=\int_{0}^{a}\frac{\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{a-x}}{\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{a-x}}dx \\ \Rightarrow \;\; 2I&=\int_{0}^{a}dx \\ \Rightarrow  \;\; 2I&=a \\ \Rightarrow \;\;  I&=a/2\end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2011:q30.title: GATE CE 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 30
pp:ce:2011:q30.question: The solution of the differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx}+\frac{y}{x}=x$, with the condition that y = 1 at x = 1, is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}+\frac{y}{x}=x, \; y\left ( 1 \right )=1$

This is a linear differential equation $\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}+Py =Q$ with $P=\frac{1}{x}$ and $Q=x$

IF = Integrating Factor

$=e^{\int Pdx}=e^{\int \frac{1}{x}dx}=e^{\ln x}=x$

Solution is,

$$\begin{aligned}  y.IF&=\int Q\left ( IF \right )dx+C \\   y.x&=\int \left ( x.x \right )dx+C \\   yx&=\int x^{2}dx+C \\   yx&=\frac{x^{3}}{3}+C \\  y&=\frac{x^{2}}{3}+\frac{C}{x} \end{aligned}$$

Now, $y(1)=1$

$\Rightarrow \; \frac{1^{2}}{3}+\frac{C}{1} =1 \; \Rightarrow \; C=\frac{2}{3}$

So the solution is $y=\frac{x^{3}}{3}+\frac{2}{3x}$

pp:ce:2011:q31.title: GATE CE 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 31
pp:ce:2011:q31.question: The value of W that results in the collapse of the beam shown in the adjoining figure and having a plastic moment capacity of $M_{P}$ is

detailed_solution.concept: Design of Steel Structures - Plastic Analysis
detailed_solution.markdown: Number os possible hinges, $n=2$ Statical Indeterminacy, $r=1$ Number of independent mechanisms, $i=n-r=2-1=1$ $$\begin{aligned} \Delta &=7\theta =3\phi\\ \text{By principle of virtual work,}&\text{ we get,}\\ W\times \Delta -M_{P}\theta -M_{P}\left ( \theta +\phi \right )&=0 \\ W\times 7\theta &=2M_{P}\theta +M_{P}\phi \\ W\times 7\theta &=2M_{P}\theta +M_{P}\times \frac{7\theta }{3} \\ 7W&=\frac{6M_{P}+7M_{P}}{3} \\ W&=\frac{13M_{P}}{21} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2011:q34.title: GATE CE 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 34
pp:ce:2011:q34.question:
Consider two RCC beams, P and Q, each having the section 400 mm x 750 mm
(effective depth, d = 750 mm) made with concrete having a $\tau _{cmax}=2.1N/mm^{2}$. For the reinforcement provided and the grade of concrete used, it may be assumed that the $\tau _{c}=0.75N/mm^{2}$. The design shear in beam P is 400 kN and in beam Q is 750 kN. Considering the provisions of IS 456-2000, which of the following statements is TRUE?
options:
Shere reinforcement should be designed for 175 kN for beam P and the
section for beam Q should be revised.

Nominal shear reinforcement is required for beam P and the shear
reinforcement should be designed for 120 kN for beam Q.

Shear reinforcement should be designed for 175 kN for beam P and the
shear reinforcement should be designed for 525 kN for beam Q.
The sections for both beams P and Q need to be revised.

primary.subtopicLabel: Shear, Torsion, Bond, Anchorage and Development Length

detailed_solution.concept: RCC Structures - Shear, Torsion, Bond, Anchorage and Development Length
detailed_solution.markdown:
Shear strength of the concrete $=\tau_{c} \times B d$

$=0.75 \times 400 \times 750 \times 10^{-3}=225 \mathrm{kN}$

Maximum shear strength of concrete

$$\begin{array}{l}

=\tau_{c \max } \times B d \\

=2.1 \times 400 \times 750 \times 10^{-3}=630 \mathrm{kN}

\end{array}$$

Design shear in beam P is 400kN which is less

than the maximum shear that the concrete can

sustain. But the design shear is more than the

nominal shear of 225 kN.

$\therefore$ Shear reinforcement is designed for

$=400-225=175 \mathrm{kN}$

Design shear in beam Q is 750 kN which is more

than the maximum shear that the concrete can

sustain. Hence the beam Q should be redesigned.

pp:ce:2011:q35.title: GATE CE 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 35
pp:ce:2011:q35.question: The figure shows a schematic representation of a steel plate girder to be used as a simply supported beam with a concentrated load. For stiffeners, PQ (running along the beam axis) and RS (running between the top and bottom flanges), which of the following pairs of statements will be TRUE?
options:
(i) RS should be provided under the concentrated load only.
(ii) PQ should be placed in the tension side of the flange.

(i) RS helps to prevent local buckling of the web.
(ii) PQ should be placed in the compression side of the flange.

(i) RS should be provided at supports.
(ii) PQ should be placed along the neutral axis.

(i) RS should be provided away from points of action of concentrated loads.
(ii) PQ should be provided on the compression side of the flange.

detailed_solution.markdown:
PQ is a horizontal stiffener in the given plate girder. Horizontal stiffeners are also called longitudinal stiffeners. The horizontal stiffener are provided in the compression zone of the web. The first horizontal stiffener is provided at one-fifth of the distance from the compression flange to the tension flange. If required another stiffener is provided at the neutral axis. Horizontal stiffeners are not continuous and are provided between vertical stiffeners.

RS is a vertical stiffener in the given plate girder. Vertical stiffeners are also called transverse stiffeners. It is assumed that the vertical stiffener is not subjected to any load and is selected to provide necessary lateral stiffness only and can therefore, br crimped or joggled for tight fittings. Such stiffeners increase the buckling resistance of the web caused by shear.

pp:ce:2011:q36.title: GATE CE 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 36
pp:ce:2011:q36.question: A singly under-reamed, 8 m long, RCC pile (shown in the figure) weighing 20 kN with 350 mm shaft diameter and 750 mm under-ream diameter is installed within stiff, saturated silty clay (undrained shear strength is 50 kPa, adhesion factor is 0.3, and the applicable bearing capacity factor is 9) to counteract the impact of soil swelling on a structure constructed above. Neglecting suction and the contribution of the under-ream to the adhesive shaft capacity, what would be the estimated ultimate tensile capacity (rounded off to the nearest integer value of kN) of the pile?

detailed_solution.markdown:
The tensile resistance of a pile is given as

$$\begin{aligned} Q_{t} &=Q_{s}+W+Q_{b} \\ \text{Where}\quad Q_{s} &=\text { shaft resistance }=\alpha c A_{s} \\ W &=\text { weight of pile } \\ Q_{1} &=c N_{c} A_{b} \\ \therefore \quad Q_{1} &=\alpha c A_{s}+W+c N_{c} A_{b} \\ &=0.3 \times 50 \times \pi \times 0.35 \times 8+20 \\ &+\frac{50 \times 9 \times \pi\left(0.75^{2}-0.35^{2}\right)}{4} \\ &=300.796 \mathrm{kN} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2011:q37.title: GATE CE 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 37
pp:ce:2011:q37.question: Identical surcharges are placed at ground surface at sites X and Y , with soil conditions shown in figure and water table at ground surface. The silty clay layers at X and Y are identical. The thin sand layer at Y is continuous and freedraining with a very large discharge capacity. If primary consolidation at X is estimated to complete in 36 months, what would be the corresponding time for completion of primary consolidation at Y ?

detailed_solution.markdown:
The time required for any degree of consolidation can be obtained from the Taylor's formula,

$T_{v}=\frac{C_{v} t}{d^{2}}$

since C_{v} is constant for same type of soil and $T_{v}$ is constant for same degree of consolidation,

$t \propto d^{2}$ where d is the length of drainage path.

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{t_{1}}{t_{2}}&=\left(\frac{d_{1}}{d_{2}}\right)^{2}\\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{36}{t_{2}}&=\left(\frac{10}{10 / 2}\right)^{2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad t_{2}&=\frac{36}{4} \\ \Rightarrow \quad t_{2}&=9 \;\text{months} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2011:q38.title: GATE CE 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 38
pp:ce:2011:q38.question: A field vane shear testing instrument (shown in figure) was inserted completely into a deposit of soft, saturated silty clay with the vane rod vertical such that the top of the blades were 500 mm below the ground surface. Upon application of a rapidly increasing torque about the vane rod, the soil was found to fail when the torque reached 4.6 Nm. Assuming mobilization of undrained shear strength on all failure surfaces to be uniform and the resistance mobilized on the surface of the vane rod to be neglibible, what would be the peak undrained shear strength (rounded off to the nearest integer value of kPa) of the soil?

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Shear Strength of Soil
detailed_solution.markdown:
When the top end of the vane completely shear the soil, Then the torque at failure is given by

$$\begin{aligned} T&=c_{u} \pi\left(\frac{d^{\prime} h}{2}+\frac{d^{3}}{6}\right)\\ \Rightarrow \frac{4.6}{1000}&=c_{u} \times \pi \times\left(\frac{(0.05)^{2} \times 0.1}{2}+\frac{(0.05)^{3}}{6}\right) \\ \Rightarrow \quad c_{u}&=10 \mathrm{kPa} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2011:q39.title: GATE CE 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 39
pp:ce:2011:q39.question:
A single pipe of length 1500 m and diameter 60 cm connects two reservoirs having
a difference of 20 m in their water levels. The pipe is to be replaced by two pipes
of the same length and equal diameter d to convey 25% more discharge under the
same head loss. If the friction factor is assumed to be the same for all the pipes,
the value of d is approximately equal to which of the following options?

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Flow Through Pipes
detailed_solution.markdown: For single pipe $$\begin{array}{r} n=\frac{81 L Q}{\pi^{2} g D^{2}} \\ L=1500 \mathrm{m}, \mathrm{D}=0.6 \mathrm{m} \\ n_{f}=20 \mathrm{m} \\ Q_{1}=\frac{0.112}{\sqrt{1}} \end{array}$$ In case of double pipe discharge is increased by 25% than that of previous case hence. $$\begin{aligned} 2Q_{2}&=1.25Q_{1}\\ 20 &= \frac{8F\times 500\times(0.625Q_{1})^{2}}{9.81\times \pi^{2}\times d^{5}}\\ Q_{1}&= \frac{0.402\times d^{5/2}}{\sqrt{f}}\\ \frac{Q_{1}^{2}}{d^{5}}&=0.413\\ Q_{1}^{2}&=\frac{0.413d^{5}}{f}\\ Q_{1}&=\frac{0.642d^{5/2}}{\sqrt{f}}\ldots\\ \text{From eq }(i) &\text{and }(ii),\text{ we get}\\ d&=437 \mathrm{cm}=50 \mathrm{cm} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2011:q40.title: GATE CE 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 40
pp:ce:2011:q40.question:
A spillway discharges flood flow at a rate of 9 $m^3$/s per metre width. If the depth
of flow on the horizontal apron at the toe of the spillway is 46 cm, the tail water
depth needed to form a hydraulic jump is approximately given by which of the
following options?

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Open Channel Flow
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{q}&=9 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{s} / \mathrm{m}\\ \text{and }y_{1}&=46 \mathrm{cm}=0.46 \mathrm{m} \\ \therefore \quad V_{1}&=\frac{q}{y_{1}}=\frac{9}{0.46}=19.565 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ F_{1}&=\frac{V_{1}}{\sqrt{g y_{1}}}=\frac{19.565}{\sqrt{9.81 \times 0.46}}=9.21 \end{aligned}$$

Thus, flow is super -critical.

Thus the sequent depth will be

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{y_{2}}{y_{1}}&=\frac{1}{2}\left[-1+\sqrt{1+8 F_{1}^{2}}\right]\\ \Rightarrow \quad y_{2}&=\frac{0.46}{2}\left[-1+\sqrt{1+8 \times(9.21)^{2}}\right] \\ \Rightarrow \quad y_{2}&=0.23 \times 25.07 \\ \Rightarrow \quad y_{2}&=5.77 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2011:q41.title: GATE CE 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 41
pp:ce:2011:q41.question:
In an aquifer extending over 150 hectare, the water table was 20m below ground
level. Over a period of time the water table dropped to 23m below the ground
level. If the porosity of aquifer is 0.40 and the specific retention is 0.15, what is
the change in ground water storage of the aquifer?

primary.subtopicLabel: Source of Water Supply, Distribution System and Well Hydraulics

detailed_solution.concept: Environmental Engineering - Source of Water Supply, Distribution System and Well Hydraulics
detailed_solution.markdown:
We know that,

$$\begin{aligned} n&=S_{y}+S_{r} \\ \Rightarrow\quad S_{y}&=S_{t}-n=0.15-0.40=-0.25 \end{aligned}$$

The negative sign signifies the decrease in storage. Change in volume of aquifer

$=150 \times(23-20)=450 \mathrm{ha}-\mathrm{m}$

Specific yield is nothing but the actual volume of water that can be extracted by force of gravity from a unit volume of aquifer.

$\therefore$Change in water storage

$=450 \times 0.25=112.5 \mathrm{ha}-\mathrm{m}$

pp:ce:2011:q42.title: GATE CE 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 42
pp:ce:2011:q42.question:
Total suspended particulate matter (TSP) concentration in ambient air is to be
measured using a high volume sampler. The filter used for this purpose had an
initial dry weight of 9.787 g. The filter was mounted in the sampler and the initial
air flow rate through the filter was set at 1.5$m^3$/min. Sampling continued for
24 hours. The airflow after 24 hours was measured to be 1.4 $m^3$/min. The dry
weight of the filter paper after 24 hour sampling was 10.283 g. Assuming a linear
decline in the air flow rate during sampling, what is the 24 hour average TSP
concentration in the ambient air?

detailed_solution.concept: Environmental Engineering - Air and Noise Pollution
detailed_solution.markdown:
Average airflow rate

$= 1.5-\left ( \frac{1.5-1.4}{24\times 60} \right )\times 12=1.45\; m^{3}/min$

Total airflow through the sampler during 24 hours

$=1.45\times 24\times 60=2088\: m^{3}$

TSP concentration in the ambient air

$=\left ( \frac{10.283-9.787}{2088} \right )\times 10^6=237.5\mu g/m^3$

pp:ce:2011:q43.title: GATE CE 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 43
pp:ce:2011:q43.question:
Chlorine gas (8 mg/L as $CI_2$) was added to a drinking water sample. If the free chlorine residual and pH was measured to be 2mg/L (as $CI_2$) and 7.5, respectively, what is the concentration of residual $OCI^{-}$ ions in the water? Assume that the chlorine gas added to the water is completely converted to HOCl and $OCI^{-}$. Atomic Weight of Cl: 35.5
Given: $OC1^{-}+H^{+}\leftrightharpoons^k HOCI, \; \; \; K=10^{7.5}$

detailed_solution.markdown:
$OCl^{-}\: +\: H^{+}\: \rightleftharpoons ^{K}\; \; HOCl;\; K=10^{7.5}$

Now,

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{\left [ HOCl \right ]}{\left [ OCl^{-} \right ]\left [ H^{+} \right ]} &= K\\ pH&=7.5 \\ \left [ H^{+} \right ]&=10^{7.5} \\ \left [ \frac{HOCl}{OCl^{-}} \right ]&=10^{7.5}\times 10^{-7.5}=1 \\ \therefore \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \left [ HOCl \right ] &=\left [ OCl^{-} \right ] \\ \left [ \text{Free chlorine residual} \right ]&=\left [ HOCl \right ]+\left [ OCl^{-} \right ] \\ \text{Free chlorine residual} &= 2\; \text{mg/l}\\ \left [ \text{Free chlorine residual} \right ] &=\frac{2\times 10^{-3}}{Mol.\; wt\; of\; Cl_{2}} \\ &=\frac{2\times 10^{-3}}{2\times 35.5} \\ &=2.817\times 10^{-5}\; \text{moles/l} \\ \therefore \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; 2.817\times 10^{-5} &=\left [ HOCl \right ]+\left [ OCl^{-} \right ] \\ \therefore \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \left [ OCl^{-} \right ] &=\frac{2.817\times 10^{-5}}{2} \\ \because \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \left [ OCl^{-} \right ] &=\left [ HOCl \right ] \\ &=1.4084\times 10^{-5}\; \text{moles/l} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2011:q48.title: GATE CE 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 48
pp:ce:2011:q48.question:
A sand layer found at sea floor under 20 m water depth is characterized with relative density=40%,
maximum void ratio=1.0 ,
minimum void ratio=0.5, and
specific gravity of soil solids=2.67.
Assume the specific gravity of sea water to be 1.03 and the unit weight of fresh water to be 9.81 kN/$m^3$.

What would be the effective stress (rounded off to the nearest integer value of kPa) at 30 m depth into the sand layer?

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Effective Stress and Permeability
detailed_solution.markdown: Relative density is given by $$\begin{aligned} I_{D}(\%)&=\left(\frac{e_{\max }-e_{\text {nat }}}{e_{\max }-e_{\min }}\right) \times 100\\ \Rightarrow \quad 40&=\left(\frac{1-e_{n a t}}{1-0.5}\right) \times 100 \\ \Rightarrow \quad 0.4 \times 0.5&=1-e_{\text {nat }} \\ \Rightarrow \quad e_{\text {nat }}&=0.8 \\ \text{Also,} \quad G_{\text {sea }}&=\frac{\gamma_{\text {sea }}}{\gamma_{w}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \gamma_{\text {sea }}&=1.03 \times 9.81 \\ \Rightarrow \quad \gamma_{\mathrm{sea}}&=10.1043 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ \end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned} \gamma_{\mathrm{sat}}&=\left(\frac{G \gamma_{sea}+\mathrm{Se}_{\text {nat }} \times \gamma_{\text {sea }}}{1+e_{\text {nat }}}\right)\\ &=\left(\frac{2.67 \times 10.1043 +1 \times 0.8 \times 10.1043}{1+0.8}\right) \\ &=19.48 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \end{aligned}$$ Total stress at the bottom of sand layer, $$\begin{aligned} \sigma &=20 \times \gamma_{\operatorname{sen}}+30 \times \gamma_{\text {sat}} \\ &=20 \times 10.1043+30 \times 19.48 \\ &=786.486 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}$$ Pore water pressure at the bottom of sand layer, $$\begin{aligned} u &=(20+30) \times 10.1043 \\ &=505.215 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}$$ Effective stress at the bottom of sand layer. $$\begin{aligned} \bar{\sigma} &=\sigma-u=786.486 -505.215 \\ &=281.271 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2011:q49.title: GATE CE 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 49
pp:ce:2011:q49.question:
A sand layer found at sea floor under 20 m water depth is characterized with relative density=40%,
maximum void ratio=1.0 ,
minimum void ratio=0.5, and
specific gravity of soil solids=2.67.
Assume the specific gravity of sea water to be 1.03 and the unit weight of fresh water to be 9.81 kN/$m^3$.

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Effective Stress and Permeability
detailed_solution.markdown: The effective stress will not alter due to change in sea water level. The total stress will increase due to increase in sea water level. The pore water pressure will also increase in the same proportion, thus nullifying the effect of each other $$\begin{aligned} \sigma &=22 \times 10.1043+30 \times 19.48 \\ &=806.695 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ u &=(22+30) \times 10.1043 \\ &=525.424 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ \therefore\quad \bar{\sigma} &=\sigma-u=806.695-525.424 \\ &=281.271 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2011:q52.title: GATE CE 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 52
pp:ce:2011:q52.question:
A rigid beam is hinged at one end and supported on linear elastic springs (both having a stiffness of 'k') at points '1' and '2', and an inclined load acts at '2', as shown

Which of the following options represents the deflections $\delta _{1} \; and \; \delta _{2}$ at points '1' and '2'?

detailed_solution.markdown: The free diagram of the beam is shown below From similar triangles, we get $$\begin{aligned} \frac{L}{\delta_{1}}=\frac{2 L}{\delta_{2}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \delta_{2}=2 \delta_{1} \quad &\ldots(i) \end{aligned}$$ Taking moments about hinge, we get $$\begin{aligned} P \times 2 L-k \delta_{2} \times 2 L-k \delta_{1} \times L&=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad 2 P-k\left(2 \delta_{2}+\delta_{1}\right)&=0 &[\therefore\text{ from(i)}]\\ \Rightarrow \quad 2 P-k\left(4 \delta_{1}+\delta_{1}\right)&=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad \delta_{1}&=\frac{2 P}{5 k} \end{aligned}$$ From (i), we get $\delta_{2}=2 \times \frac{2 P}{5 k}=\frac{4 P}{5 k}$

pp:ce:2011:q53.title: GATE CE 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 53
pp:ce:2011:q53.question:
A rigid beam is hinged at one end and supported on linear elastic springs (both having a stiffness of 'k') at points '1' and '2', and an inclined load acts at '2', as shown

If the load P equals 100 kN, which of the following options represents forces R1 and R2 in the springs at points '1' and '2'?

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} R_{1} &=k \delta_{1}=k \times \frac{2 P}{5 k} \\ &=\frac{2 \times 100}{5}=40 \mathrm{kN} \\ R_{2} &=k \delta_{2}=k \times \frac{4 P}{5 k} \\ &=\frac{4 \times 100}{5}=80 \mathrm{kN} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2011:q54.title: GATE CE 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 54
pp:ce:2011:q54.question:
The sludge from the aeration tank of the activated sludge process (ASP) has solids content (by weight) of 2%. This sludge is put in a sludge thickener, where sludge volume is reduced to half. Assume that the amount of solids in the supernatant from the thickener is negligible, the specific gravity of sludge solids is 2.2 and the density of water is 1000 $kg/m^{3}$.

What is the density of the sludge removed from the aeration tank?

detailed_solution.concept: Environmental Engineering - Treatment of Waste Water
detailed_solution.markdown:
2 % of solids +98 % water $\rightarrow$ 100 % of sludge

let x be the density of sludge.

$$\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad \frac{100}{x}&=\frac{98}{1000}+\frac{2}{2.2 \times 1000} \\ &\quad \quad \ldots\text{ Harmonic mean }\\ \therefore \quad x&=1011 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{ms} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2011:q55.title: GATE CE 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 55
pp:ce:2011:q55.question:
The sludge from the aeration tank of the activated sludge process (ASP) has solids content (by weight) of 2%. This sludge is put in a sludge thickener, where sludge volume is reduced to half. Assume that the amount of solids in the supernatant from the thickener is negligible, the specific gravity of sludge solids is 2.2 and the density of water is 1000 $kg/m^{3}$.

What is the solids content (by weight) of the thickened sludge?

detailed_solution.concept: Environmental Engineering - Treatment of Waste Water
detailed_solution.markdown:
Now,

$$\begin{aligned} V_{1} &=\text { Volume of sludge (initial) } \\ &=\text { Volume of solids }+\text { Volume of } w \\ &=\frac{2}{2.2 \times 1000}+\frac{98}{1000} \\ V_{1} &=0.0989 \mathrm{m}^{3} \end{aligned}$$

Volume of sludge after thickness

$$\begin{aligned} &=V_{2}=\frac{V_{1}}{2} \\ V_{2} &=0.04945 \mathrm{m}^{3}\\ \therefore \quad 0.04945&= \text{ Vol. of solids }+\text{ Vol. of water}\\ \therefore \quad 0.04945&=\frac{2}{2.2 \times 1000}+\frac{x}{1000} \\ \therefore \quad x&=48.545 \% \end{aligned}$$

$\therefore \text{ Solids content }(%\text{ by Wt.})$

$$\begin{array}{l} =\frac{2}{2+48.545} \times 100 \\ =3.957 \% \\ \approx 3.96 \% \end{array}$$
